beliefs: For x>=1 the fit is exact to rounding: x^3+2^x+22 at x=3 gives 28401.19, matching f(3) [E2,E4]
So the same formula x^3+2^x+22 holds on both sides; the earlier 'mirror' idea was wrong [E1,E4]
The only anomaly is on the interval 0<x<1: f(0.25)=-3.2851, f(0.5)=-21.9553, f(0.75)=-14.0279, while x^3+2^x+22 gives ~23-24 there [E5]
At x=0 f(0)=22.28, close to but not exactly 23 (x^3+2^x+22 at 0 = 23); small offset ~-0.72 [E1,E5]
At x=1 f(1)=70.35 matches x^3+2^x+22=25? no: 1+2+22=25, but observed 70.35, so the formula must be re-examined at x=1 [E5]?

Recheck: x^3+2^x+22 at x=1 = 25, but f(1)=70.35; at x=2 = 8+4+22=34, but f(2)=3783.82 — so the formula is NOT x^3+2^x+22; likely 2^x dominates with a different exponent base or x^3 coefficient [E1,E4]?
f(1)=70.35, f(2)=3783.82, f(4)=118359.4: ratios 53.8, 31.3 — not pure exponential; cubic+exponential still plausible with different constant [E1]?
The interval 0<x<1 has negative values dipping to -21.96 at x=0.5, unlike the rest of the domain which is positive for x>=0 [E5]
Best current guess: f(x)=x^3+2^x+22 for x>=1 and x<0, but on (0,1) something subtracts a large bump, and the constant may be ~22.28 not 22 [E5]?
notes: E5 shows the (0,1) interval has strongly negative values, confirming a special interval there. Also re-examining E1/E4: x^3+2^x+22 does NOT match f(1)=70.35 or f(2)=3783.82 (predicts 25 and 34), so the base formula is wrong; the values grow much faster, suggesting a different exponential or coefficient. I keep the piecewise structure but flag the base formula as uncertain.
